title: Buying Land in Benin City: What to Check Before You Pay
excerpt: A practical checklist for land buyers — from title documents and survey plans to visiting the site and paying safely.
body:
Land is one of the most popular ways to own property in Benin City, and one of the easiest to get wrong. A few careful checks before you pay can save years of disputes.

## Confirm who is selling
Ask for the seller's identity and their right to sell. If the seller is a family, find out who is authorised to sign on the family's behalf. If it is a company or estate developer, ask for its registration details.

## Review the documents
Ask to see the title documents and the survey plan. A survey plan shows the exact boundaries and should be checked against government records to confirm the land is not under acquisition or set aside for public use. In Edo State, title and land information is handled by the state's land registry and geographic information service.

## Visit the land
Always inspect in person, or have someone you trust inspect for you. Walk the boundaries, look for beacons, talk to neighbours and check how the land is accessed in the rainy season.

## Use a lawyer
A property lawyer can run searches, draft or review the deed of assignment, and guide you through registering your interest. This is money well spent.

## Pay safely
- Pay into a verifiable account in the seller's or company's name
- Get receipts for every payment
- Do not pay in full before the documents have been reviewed

This article is general information, not legal advice. Speak to Pablo Homes about available land, and to a qualified lawyer before you commit.

title: Renting in Benin City: Questions to Ask Before You Pay
excerpt: Rent is often paid a year or more in advance, so it pays to ask the right questions first.
body:
Because rent is often paid a year or more in advance, choosing the wrong apartment is an expensive mistake. Here are the questions worth asking before you commit.

## What does the total cost include?
Ask for a clear breakdown of everything you will pay at the start: rent, any service charge, and any agency, legal or caution fees. Ask which of these are refundable.

## What is covered by the service charge?
In serviced buildings, find out exactly what the service charge pays for — power backup, water, security, waste collection, cleaning of shared areas — and how it is reviewed.

## How are power and water supplied?
Check the meter type, how backup power works, and where water comes from. Turn on taps and switches during the inspection.

## Who handles repairs?
Agree in writing who is responsible for what, and how quickly issues are attended to.

## What does the tenancy agreement say?
Read it in full before paying. Look at the duration, renewal terms, notice periods and house rules.

## Visit at different times
If you can, see the area in the evening and after rain. Traffic, noise and drainage can look very different at different times.

Browse rentals on the Pablo Homes website, or book an inspection and bring this list with you.

title: How Property Inspections Work — and How to Get the Most from One
excerpt: What to expect when you book an inspection, and a simple checklist to take with you.
body:
An inspection is your chance to see a property as it really is. A little preparation makes it far more useful.

## Booking
Request an inspection from any listing on this website by choosing a preferred date and time. Your booking is a request until Pablo Homes confirms the appointment with you by phone or WhatsApp.

## Before you go
- Shortlist what matters most: rooms, parking, power, water, commute
- Prepare questions about price, documents and payment terms
- Bring a tape measure and charge your phone for photos and video

## During the inspection
Check walls and ceilings for damp or cracks, open windows and doors, test taps and switches, and look at the drainage around the building. For land, walk the boundaries and look for beacons.

## After the inspection
Write down your impressions while they are fresh. If you are interested, ask for the documents to review with your lawyer before making any payment.

## Can't attend in person?
If you live outside Benin City or abroad, ask whether a live video walkthrough can be arranged, and consider sending a trusted representative as well.

title: Buying Property in Nigeria from Abroad: A Practical Guide
excerpt: Distance makes due diligence more important, not less. Here is how to buy carefully from the UK, US, Canada or anywhere else.
body:
Many Nigerians in the diaspora want a home or an investment back home. Buying from a distance is very possible — it just needs more structure.

## Work with people you can verify
Deal with businesses whose phone numbers, office location and track record you can check independently. Be cautious of offers that feel rushed or too good to be true.

## See the property — even remotely
Ask for recent photos and video, a live video walkthrough, and if possible a visit by a trusted family member or friend. For land, ask for the survey plan and confirm the coordinates.

## Instruct your own lawyer
Appoint a property lawyer in Nigeria who acts for you, not the seller. Your lawyer can run searches, review documents and handle the transfer paperwork.

## Understand the full cost
Beyond the price, budget for legal fees, registration and consent costs, and any agency fees. Ask for every cost in writing.

## Keep a paper trail
- Pay only into verifiable accounts in the seller's name
- Keep receipts, agreements and messages
- Avoid cash handovers through third parties

Pablo Homes can share listing details, photos and video, and arrange inspections for you or your representative. Start by requesting details on any property.

title: Off-Plan Property: Understanding the Trade-Offs
excerpt: Off-plan can mean a lower entry price and staged payments — and it also carries real risks. Here is how to weigh them.
body:
Buying off-plan means committing to a property before it is built. It is common in growing cities, and it suits some buyers well — but it is important to understand both sides.

## Why buyers consider off-plan
- The entry price is often lower than for a completed home
- Payments are usually spread over the construction period
- You may be able to choose a unit or finishes early

## The risks to weigh
- Construction can be delayed
- The finished home may differ from the plans or renders
- The value of the property on completion is not guaranteed

## Questions to ask
Who is the developer, and what have they delivered before? Are the title documents and building approvals in place? What happens to your payments if the project is delayed? What exactly is included in the finish?

## Protect yourself
Have a lawyer review the contract of sale before you pay, make sure the payment schedule is linked to construction progress, and visit the site during the build.

Pablo Homes lists off-plan opportunities where available. Treat every listing as a starting point for your own due diligence.

title: Understanding Property Documents in Nigeria
excerpt: A plain-English introduction to the documents you are likely to hear about when buying property.
body:
Property documents can be confusing. Here is a plain-English introduction to the ones you are most likely to hear about. Always have a lawyer confirm what applies to a specific property.

## Certificate of Occupancy (C of O)
Issued by the state government, a C of O evidences a right to occupy land for a stated term. It is one of the strongest title documents for land in Nigeria.

## Governor's Consent
When land that already has a C of O changes hands, the new owner registers the transaction by obtaining the Governor's Consent.

## Survey plan
A survey plan, prepared by a registered surveyor, shows the exact location and boundaries of the land. It should be charted to confirm the land is not subject to government acquisition.

## Deed of assignment
This is the agreement that transfers the seller's interest in the property to the buyer. It should be properly drafted, signed, stamped and registered.

## Receipts and agreements
Keep receipts for every payment and copies of every agreement. They form part of your record of ownership.

This is general information, not legal advice. Ask Pablo Homes about the documents available for any listed property, and review them with your lawyer.
